claims.text: A Pod created on its own (no owner/controller) is not recreated after kubectl delete pod; it stays NotFound until its manifest is applied again.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Pods (Pods and controllers; 'Pods are not designed to be self-healing'); outputs/stage-2/scripts/k8s/replicaset.txt

claims.text: A ReplicaSet maintains a stable set of replica Pods: it is defined by a selector, a replicas number and a pod template, creates Pods from the template when there are too few matching Pods and deletes Pods when there are too many.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Workloads > ReplicaSet (How a ReplicaSet works)

claims.text: The ReplicaSet's control loop (ReplicaSet controller in kube-controller-manager, on the control plane) repeatedly compares replicas with the number of matching Pods and works through the API server.
spec.template has the same schema as a Pod, nested, without apiVersion and kind; Pods created from it get the template's labels.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: ReplicaSet (Pod Template); Workloads > Pods (Pod templates)

claims.text: spec.template.metadata.labels must match spec.selector or the API server rejects the ReplicaSet: 'selector does not match template labels' (seen with kubectl apply --dry-run=server).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: ReplicaSet (Pod Selector: must match or be rejected by the API); outputs/stage-2/scripts/k8s/replicaset.txt

claims.text: kubectl apply --dry-run=server sends the object to the API server for validation and admission without persisting it.
claims.source_hint: kubectl apply reference (--dry-run=server); kubernetes.io API concepts (Dry-run)

claims.text: A replacement Pod is a new Pod named after the ReplicaSet plus a random suffix (generateName) and is assigned its own IP address; nothing reserves the deleted Pod's address for it.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: ReplicaSet; Pod lifecycle (Pods are not rescheduled; replaced by new Pod with new UID); outputs replicaset.txt

claims.text: Changing replicas and applying again makes the ReplicaSet create or delete Pods to reach the new number.
Changing only a ReplicaSet's pod template does not change Pods already running; only Pods created afterwards use the new template.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: ReplicaSet (Deleting just a ReplicaSet / 'the new Pod template will not affect existing Pods'); outputs replicaset.txt

claims.text: kubectl get replicaset shows DESIRED, CURRENT (.status.replicas: its non-terminating Pods) and READY (those of them that are ready); for web after apply they read 3 3 3.
deploy/k8s/lessons/web-replicaset.yaml@stage-2: ReplicaSet web in donhang, replicas 3, selector.matchLabels app: web, template labels app: web (line 18), container caddy:2.10.0 port 80.

replicaset.sh@stage-2 applies web-pod.yaml (line 11, re-creating web if gone) then deletes it, applies the ReplicaSet, deletes one Pod, dry-runs a template labelled app: website, applies replicas 4 + caddy:2.10.2 via sed | kubectl apply -f -; helpers at lines 8-9; output replicaset.txt.
kubectl get -o wide adds columns including the Pod IP; kubectl delete pods -l app=web -n donhang deletes all matching Pods.
